messages:
Devon: taking over evening coverage now, leaving a short runbook of odd signals I was watching :wave:
Devon: summary: brief encoder-small CPU thrash, KV TTL skew in eu, and two quick router backlog pulses. no user errors observed yet
Marta: saw the CPU spike at ~19:03 UTC too, latency tail bumped for ~45s
Devon: yep. looks correlated to big coalesced batches from the load-tester. batch coalescer tried to merge many small requests and overloaded encoder-small
Alex: can we gate the coalescer or add a per-pool batch cap?
Devon: plan: set ENCODER_MAX_COALESCE=8 for encoder-small in runtime config and push to canary. command i'll run: `kubectl -n inference set env ds/encoder-runtime ENCODER_MAX_COALESCE=8`
Sam: +1. also consider a short cooldown window for the coalescer so it doesn't reattempt immediately
Jen: pro-tip: encoder_cpu_spike alert is currently 1m eval, which is noisy for these spikes. suggest 3m sustained before firing
Devon: noted, i'll draft an alert change PR and add the reasoning
oncall-bot: rotation update: Devon -> Alex (primary) / Marta (backup) until 03:30 UTC
Marta: FYI: observed kv_replication_ttl_skew ~12s in eu for the past 10m. filing ticket after handoff
Alex: that could explain some prefix-cache miss bursts we saw earlier. if replicas lag TTL checks, stale entries get evicted unevenly
Devon: action: Marta to file infra ticket RI-1487 and ping infra team in morning; i'll add a temporary alert to track kv_ttl_skew > 10s
Marta: filing now: https://redwood.internal/issue/RI-1487 - KV TTL skew (eu)
Devon: router: router_queue_depth spiked twice to ~250 but drained in <90s during autoscaler warmup
Alex: we should document manual fallback for oncall: if queue >200 for >3m and p95 latency >500ms, escalate and flip traffic to dedicated-tier. link to runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/route-fallback
Jen: automation note: we don't have a safe auto-flip yet. i'll prototype a route-by-latency rule tomorrow but leave manual for tonight
Devon: ops checklist for whoever's oncall: 1) watch encoder CPU p95 and queue depth 2) watch kv_replication_ttl_skew 3) watch router queue depth & p95
Devon: quick commands: check encoder pods: `kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=encoder-small -o wide`
Devon: check kv lag: `SELECT avg(lag_seconds) FROM kv_replication WHERE region='eu' AND ts > now() - interval '5 minutes'`
Sam: if spikes persist after coalesce cap, consider temporarily bumping encoder-small min_replicas +1 (safe short-term mitigation)
Devon: agree. i'll monitor for 15m post-rollout and escalate if needed
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: encoder-runtime env ENCODER_MAX_COALESCE=8
deploy-bot: Canary deploy succeeded - 2/2 encoder-small pods rolled, health checks OK
Devon: monitoring 15m windows now. will post updates if regressions
Alex: if anything nasty happens overnight, ping @pager or call the oncall phone. I'll be primary until 03:30 UTC
Marta: standby as backup, will pick up tickets in morning for KV TTL follow-up
Jen: added encoder mitigation steps to alert runbook and will open the PR to bump alert duration
Devon: handing off. react with :eyes: if you take any mitigation action so we don't duplicate effort
Alex: got it, thanks Devon :thumbsup:
Marta: thanks, handoff clear
Devon: logging handoff complete
